transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me today. I... well, I hope I'm not making a fuss over nothing, really. It's just that, lately, my head has been feeling a little bit... foggy? I suppose that's the best word for it. 

I just keep mixing up simple things, which is terribly embarrassing. You know, silly little things like appointment times, or the dates for the exhibits I help out with, or even forgetting which volunteer I’ve already called on the phone. I'm sure it's probably just me getting a bit older and it's nothing to worry about, right? Is... is that the sort of thing I should be telling you? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
How long have you been experiencing this foggy feeling in your head?

Oh, goodness, let me think... I suppose it's been about four months now? Yes, right around four months. It seemed to start right after we had some terrible water damage at the house, which, well, it pushed us into doing a whole remodel. 

It's been quite a chaotic time with all of that going on, so I just assumed the stress of the mess was making me a little scatterbrained. Anyone would get a bit mixed up with contractors coming and going and things being out of place, wouldn't they? I mean, it's not too unusual to feel a little distracted under those circumstances, is it? I just hope I'm not wasting your time with all of this.
Have you been feeling anxious or depressed lately?

Oh, goodness, no. I wouldn't say I've been depressed at all. I've always tried to keep a positive outlook on things, you know? And as for being anxious... well, I suppose I fret a little bit about the house getting finished, but just the normal amount anyone would! Nothing serious. 

I certainly don't want to sound like a complainer, because I really do have so much to be thankful for. It's really just this silly fogginess that's been bothering me. Is... is that what you were asking? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.
Have you noticed any difficulty remembering things that happened before the water damage and remodel?

Oh, no, Doctor. No, I don't think so at all. My memory for things before all that mess started is... well, it's clear as a bell, really! I can remember all of that perfectly fine. 

It's truly just the recent, day-to-day little details that seem to slip away from me right now. I hope that's a good sign? I mean, if I can remember the past just fine, that means it's nothing too terrible, right? Am I answering your questions all right? I just want to make sure I'm being helpful to you.
Do you ever feel confused about where you are or what time of day it is?

Oh, heavens, no. No, nothing like that. I always know exactly where I am, and... well, I keep a very reliable routine, so I always know what time of day it is. I might misplace my reading glasses here and there with all the house chaos, but I certainly haven't forgotten where I am or anything frightening like that! 

I try very hard to stay sharp and keep on top of things, you know. I hope that's helpful for you to know? I just wouldn't want you to think I'm, well, losing my mind or anything. I'm doing okay with all these questions, aren't I?
Do you ever feel disoriented or unsure about the date?

Oh, my, no. I keep a very close eye on the calendar. I have one right in the kitchen, and I make a point to cross off the days every single morning with my coffee, so... no, I'm never really unsure about the date. 

I mean, maybe once in a blue moon I'll have to pause and think if it's the 14th or the 15th, but just normal little things like that! Nothing where I'm truly disoriented or lost, I promise. I try to be very good about staying on top of things like that. Is... is that helpful? I'm trying my very best to give you the right information, I just want to be sure I'm doing a good job for you.
Have you been feeling more tired than usual lately?

Well, maybe just a little bit, but I'm sure it's just my age, you know? It's nothing to worry about. I do find that... well, I wake up feeling a bit tired, even if I've slept through the night. And then, by the time I've washed my face and put together a little breakfast, I sometimes feel like I just need to sit down for a moment and catch my breath. 

But really, it's just a little extra resting here and there. Everyone slows down a bit at 79, don't they? I'm still keeping up with what I need to do. I hope that's the kind of answer you were looking for? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of how things are.
Have you been having trouble learning new things, like a new skill or a new routine?

Oh, goodness, no. I mean, I suppose I don't have to learn too many brand-new routines at my age, being retired and all. But... well, when something does come up, I do just fine! Like, my daughter got me a new microwave recently, with all these fancy buttons, and I picked it up right away. I just wrote down a little note on an index card to be safe, but I haven't had any real trouble learning it. 

I always try my best to keep my mind sharp, you know. I do my little word puzzles every afternoon. I certainly wouldn't say I'm struggling with learning things. Does... does that answer your question alright? I just want to be sure I'm giving you exactly what you need.
Do you have trouble focusing or paying attention to things?

Well... I suppose maybe just a little bit. I'm a little embarrassed to admit it, but... it's actually sort of what brought me in to see you today. My head just feels a bit... well, foggy, I guess you could say. 

I try so hard to stay on top of everything, but I keep mixing up these silly, simple things. Like, oh, appointment times, or the dates for the exhibits where I help out. I even forgot which volunteer I had already called on the phone the other day! It's nothing terrible, I promise, just a few little mix-ups here and there. I hope that doesn't make me sound completely scatterbrained to you... I just want to make sure I'm being perfectly honest so you have all the right details. Does that make sense? I hope I'm answering your questions alright.
Do you ever find yourself struggling to find the right words when trying to express your thoughts or have trouble explaining things to others?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say I struggle with that. I mean, everyone has a moment where a word is right on the tip of their tongue, don't they? Especially at 79! But I can always get my point across just fine. 

I still have lovely conversations with my daughter and the other ladies at the exhibit. Sometimes I might take a tiny pause just to make sure I'm saying exactly what I mean, but I certainly wouldn't call it a struggle. I hope that's alright? I just want to make sure I'm being helpful and giving you the right kind of answers. I'm doing okay so far, aren't I?
Have you noticed any changes in your daily routines or behaviors over the past four months?

Well... I suppose things have changed just a tiny bit, but nothing to worry too much about, I promise. I did mention getting a little mixed up earlier, and... well, I am a bit embarrassed to admit it, but I have accidentally missed a couple of doctor visits recently. They just completely slipped my mind! 

And the schedule at the senior center... oh dear, I tangled it up quite a bit. My husband, bless him, has had to step in and help me out with the phone calls and keeping the calendars straight. He’s even had to take over making decisions about house repairs, which I always used to handle myself. 

I feel terrible putting that on him, but it's just a little extra help for now. I don't want you to think I'm completely helpless or anything! I'm still doing my very best. Is... is that the sort of thing you were asking about? I just want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you need. Am I doing okay answering your questions?
Have you noticed a decrease in your interest in activities you used to enjoy?

Well... oh, I hate to sound like a complainer, and I'm sure it's just a silly phase, but... yes, I suppose I have. It's a little embarrassing to admit, because I’ve always prided myself on keeping so busy and active. 

But lately... well, things I used to absolutely love, like my watercolors, or tending to my tomato plants... even going line dancing or just sitting and watching the cardinals out back... they all just sort of sit there now. I look at them and I just... I can't quite make myself care about them the way I ought to. 

I feel so guilty saying that out loud! I really should be more appreciative of my hobbies and my time. I hope it's alright that I'm telling you this? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the honest truth, like you asked. Am I giving you the right kind of details?
Have you been feeling sad or empty most of the time lately?

Oh, goodness, no. I wouldn't say that at all. I mean, we all have our down days, don't we? Especially when the weather is gloomy or, you know, when you're just feeling a bit tired. But sad or empty? No, I don't think so. 

I still have my husband, and my daughter visits, and I have a very nice life, really. I certainly wouldn't want to sound ungrateful by complaining about feeling sad when I have so much to be thankful for. I try to keep a smile on, you know? 

I hope that's the right answer? I just want to make sure I'm giving you a clear picture of how things are. I'm not making things too confusing for you, am I?
Have you noticed any difficulty with making decisions or solving problems lately?

Well... I suppose that's actually sort of what brought me in to see you, if I'm being perfectly honest. I hate to make a fuss, but my head just feels a bit... foggy lately. 

It's nothing terrible, I'm sure! Just little things. Like I mentioned before, I keep mixing up simple details. I'll get confused about appointment times, or the dates for the art exhibits at the center... or even forgetting which volunteer I've already called on the phone. It's so silly of me, really. 

I just feel awful when I make those little mistakes, because I don't want to let anyone down or be a bother. I've always been so organized! Is... is that helpful for you to know? I hope I'm not oversharing or making it sound worse than it is. I just want to be a good patient and give you the right information. Did I explain that okay?
Have you lost any weight unintentionally over the past few months?

Well... oh dear, I suppose I have a little bit. I really don't want to sound like I'm not taking care of myself, because I do try my best! But... yes, I think my clothes are fitting a bit differently. 

My skirts have gotten noticeably loose lately, and it's certainly not because I've been on a diet or anything like that. I just haven't had much of an appetite, if I'm being truthful. Most days, I just sort of pick at a piece of toast or maybe have a little bowl of soup. Food just hasn't sounded very appealing to me, which is so strange because I used to love cooking a nice meal for my husband. 

I feel terrible admitting that, like I'm wasting good food or not being a good wife by making sure we have proper dinners. I do hope you don't think poorly of me for it. Is that the sort of thing you needed to know? I want to make sure I'm answering your questions properly.
Do you feel like your thinking has slowed down lately?

Oh, goodness, no, I wouldn't say my thinking has slowed down. I mean... I mentioned the fogginess before, and being a little forgetful, but my thoughts themselves? They seem perfectly fine, really. 

If anything, I try to keep my mind active! I do my crosswords, and I read the paper... I certainly don't feel like I'm moving in slow motion or anything like that. I just have those silly little mix-ups with the schedule sometimes. 

I hope that makes sense? I wouldn't want you to think I'm losing my wits entirely! I'm just trying to be as accurate as I can for you. Did that answer your question all right?
Have you noticed any significant decline in your ability to perform daily tasks on your own without assistance?

Well... I try to do everything myself, I really do. I've always taken such pride in keeping our household running smoothly. But... oh, I hate to admit this, it's a bit embarrassing. If I'm being completely honest, my husband has had to step in just a little bit lately. 

It's nothing major, I promise! But... like I mentioned earlier about the senior center, I tangled up their schedule so badly... and I've even missed a couple of my own doctor visits, which is just dreadful of me. I really should know better. So my husband has been helping out with the phone calls and keeping the calendars straight for me. He's even had to take over making decisions about some house repairs that I always used to handle all on my own. 

I feel like such a burden to him when I can't manage my own tasks, and I hate being a nuisance. I hope that's not too terrible to admit? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the full picture so you can do your job. Is... is that what you were asking about?
Do you think your memory or thinking abilities have changed significantly over the past four months?

Oh, well... yes, I suppose that's actually the main reason my husband and I decided I should come see you. I really hate to make a fuss, and I try my very best to stay sharp, but... my head has just felt a bit foggy lately. 

I've been mixing up such simple things, and it makes me feel so terribly foolish. Like I was saying earlier about the schedules... I'll get my appointment times completely wrong, or mix up the dates for the exhibits, or I'll completely forget which volunteer I've already called on the telephone. 

I've always prided myself on being so organized, so it's quite embarrassing to admit I'm making these silly mistakes. I do hope you don't think I'm just letting myself go to pieces! I just want to be helpful and give you the right answers so you can do your job. Did I explain that clearly enough for you?
Have you been feeling hopeless about the future lately?

Oh, my, no. No, I wouldn't say that at all. I really try my very best to keep a positive outlook on things. Even with these silly little mix-ups I've been having, I certainly don't feel hopeless. 

I know I have so much to be grateful for, especially with my husband being so supportive of me lately. I'd hate to be a gloomy sort of person, you know? I always try to look on the bright side so I'm pleasant to be around for my family. 

I hope that's a good thing? I certainly don't mean to brush off your question, I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of information. Did that answer what you were looking for?
Have you been feeling irritable lately?

Well... oh dear, this is a bit hard to admit. I really do try to be a pleasant person, I truly do. But... well, when all the house repairs first started, I actually felt quite wonderful. I had so much energy, just charged up and ready to tackle everything! 

But... oh, I'm so embarrassed to say this... I suppose I did get a little bit... snappy? Just a tiny bit. If my husband or one of those sweet young volunteers at the center tried to question my plans or tell me to slow down, I would just... well, I might have bitten their heads off a little. 

I feel terrible about it, I really do. It's not like me at all to be cross with people. I just felt so sure of how things needed to be done, and I didn't want anyone getting in the way of my projects. I hope you don't think I'm a dreadful person for acting that way? I'm usually much more patient, I promise. Is... is that the sort of thing you needed to know?
